#### Input: D_select

- **IAM's name:** D_select
- **In the field's terms:** Methyltransferase site selectivity (odds of marking the correct site over a wrong one; sets the off-target stray-methylation rate)
- **Definition:** Simulator lever: cell simulator lever 'writer': D_select = 60.0 odds right site over wrong. In the chain: card D.
- **What it does:** D_select sets the odds that the writer puts a mark at the right site rather than a wrong one (60.0 odds right over wrong); this value is the D used in the the writer's stray-mark rate formula u = 1/(1 + D).
- **Why the instrument needs it:** Register the writer's stray-mark rate: the writer sometimes puts a mark where none belongs; choosing the right site over 60 wrong ones gives about one stray mark in 61 (u = 1/(1 + D), D = 60 -> 0.0164).
- **How it is obtained or computed:** D_select = 60.0 odds right site over wrong, entered on card D; it is basis 'measured' and feeds directly into the writer's stray-mark rate's formula u = 1/(1 + D), D = 60 -> 0.0164.
- **Where it is read:** not genome-located
- **Where IAM's Law enters:** This sits in IAM's Law, link 1 (actualization: each write is one sudden write of a record), long form section 1, whose text states it is 'the moment a bit becomes part of the record.' Its basis/status as given is 'measured' (set per cell type or fixed, from a cited measurement); the downstream quantity it feeds, the writer's stray-mark rate, carries status 'ACCOUNTED, meter-corrected in blood (lead, 2026-11-15) (was: ACCOUNTED (measured)'.
- **Long-form section:** link 1: long form section 1
- **Healthy value and how it is set:** Its value is fixed at 60.0 odds right site over wrong, basis 'measured', source_kind 'set per cell type or fixed, from a cited measurement'; no separate healthy range is given for this input itself.
- **Where its value comes from:** set per cell type or fixed, from a cited measurement
- **Its setting on IAM's Law Sphere:** D
- **Lever range (what moves, by how much):** open: not written yet
- **Limits and what is open:** Register the writer's stray-mark rate status as recorded: 'ACCOUNTED, meter-corrected in blood (lead, 2026-11-15) (was: ACCOUNTED (measured' (truncated). Further limits: open: not in the records yet.
- **Credit:** IAM (this work): measured by the chain on the IAM Sequencing Atlas libraries

#### Input: conv_fail

- **IAM's name:** conv_fail (the 'conv' card lever)
- **In the field's terms:** Bisulfite non-conversion rate (conversion failure rate)
- **Definition:** A simulator input lever in IAM's cell simulator, card conv, set to the value 0.0044 per non-CpG cytosine; it represents false methylation calls produced by the bisulfite conversion/sequencing chemistry itself rather than true held marks.
- **What it does:** It enters card conv and combines with tc_err to form the stray-mark rate after the meter's own false marks's 'meter' quantity, meter = conv_fail + tc_err (about 0.0044 + 0.00046), the meter's own false-mark rate.
- **Why the instrument needs it:** The instrument needs it so that the stray-mark rate after the meter's own false marks can take the writer's stray-mark rate and subtract the meter's own false marks (bisulfite conversion plus sequencing error), i.e. so the chain can separate a genuinely held methyl mark from one the sequencing chemistry fakes.
- **How it is obtained or computed:** Formula given in the packet: conv_fail = 0.0044 per non-CpG cytosine. Basis: measured. Source_kind: set per cell type or fixed, from a cited measurement.
- **Where it is read:** not genome-located
- **Where IAM's Law enters:** law_part is explicitly 'not the law: instrument or meter', and lf_section is 'not part of IAM's Law'. This is not a step in IAM's Law; it is an instrument/meter quantity recorded in the stray-mark rate after the meter's own false marks, used to correct the law-relevant measurement for sequencing-chemistry artifacts, not to derive it.
- **Long-form section:** not part of IAM's Law
- **Healthy value and how it is set:** Its value is set to 0.0044 per non-CpG cytosine (basis: measured; source_kind: set per cell type or fixed, from a cited measurement). Per the stray-mark rate after the meter's own false marks, it combines with tc_err (about 0.00046) to give the meter's total false-mark rate, described as a quarter to a third of the raw stray rate.
- **Where its value comes from:** set per cell type or fixed, from a cited measurement
- **Its setting on IAM's Law Sphere:** conv
- **Lever range (what moves, by how much):** open: not written yet
- **Limits and what is open:** open: not in the records yet
- **Credit:** IAM (this work): measured by the chain on the IAM Sequencing Atlas libraries

### 20. Serial samples from one person

- **In the field's terms:** Longitudinal comparison: the person as their own control
- **Reads from:** both: an earlier draw as a molecule file (--prior-pat) or as counts (--prior-betas), each instrument as its own input
- **What it measures and how:** A later sample against an earlier one of the same person at every CpG both measured.
- **Where IAM's Law enters:** Not the law: a chain rule.
- **Tool borrowed from cosmology:** Repeat observations of the same field (difference imaging).
- **Credit:** Difference imaging: Alard C. & Lupton R.H. (1998) ApJ 503:325-331. The within-person comparison at every shared CpG is IAM's method.
- **Methods it uses (established, not IAM's Law):** Difference imaging (subtracting a matched earlier image of the same field) (Alard C. & Lupton R.H. (1998) A method for optimal image subtraction. ApJ 503:325-331, doi 10.1086/305984)

#### Serial samples: a later sample against the same person's earlier one

*Status:* not part of the sequencing readiness check (needs a prior sample of the same person)

- **How it works:** With --prior-pat, the later sample is read against the same person's earlier sample at every site both measured.
- **Why:** The person is their own reference: no healthy reference group needed.
- **Physics:** Not IAM's Law: a chain rule.
- **Where the data comes from:** Two molecule files of the same person.
- **The numbers:** Not yet tested: public repeated-draw data are held for its test.
- **Method and standard:** Site-by-site change between draws (test owed).
- **Known-answer test:** Owed.
- **Limits:** Not part of this sign-off.
- **Where the result goes:** bundle change between draws.
- **Code:** run_sample.py (--prior-pat)
- **How to rebuild it:** Read both files; compare at shared sites.
- **History:** Dated entries in the development log (METHYLPHYS_DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md) and the instrument's development record.
- **Files in the repository:** [run_sample.py](https://github.com/hmahaffeyges/IAM-Validation/blob/main/Biological_Physics/MethylPhys/chain/MethylPhys_Interface/run_sample.py), [decoder_text.md](https://github.com/hmahaffeyges/IAM-Validation/blob/main/Biological_Physics/MethylPhys/manual/decoder_text.md), [MethylPhys_CPG_SOP_v4.md](https://github.com/hmahaffeyges/IAM-Validation/blob/main/Biological_Physics/MethylPhys/sop/MethylPhys_CPG_SOP_v4.md), [METHYLPHYS_DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md](https://github.com/hmahaffeyges/IAM-Validation/blob/main/Biological_Physics/MethylPhys/METHYLPHYS_DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md)

*Questions a researcher will ask:*

- **What exactly is this test comparing?** It compares a later sample from a person against an earlier sample from that same person, looking at every CpG site that both samples happened to measure. *(Evidence: instrument record: field_how)*
- **Why use the person's own earlier sample instead of comparing against a panel of healthy people?** Because the person acts as their own reference point, so a separate healthy reference group isn't needed for this comparison. *(Evidence: instrument record: rule 'why' explanation)*
- **Is this comparison based on some established statistical law?** No. It is a comparison rule of the pipeline: the person's earlier sample serves as the reference; IAM's Law does not enter it. *(Evidence: instrument record: law field)*
- **What are the limitations of this method that I should know about before relying on it?** Not yet recorded: the limits of serial comparison (how far apart the samples may be, and how depth differences are handled) have not been written for this instrument. *(Evidence: instrument record: rule 'limits' field)*

- **Reads from:** candidates: set when built (the plasma fragment tail would need molecules with their fragment ends)
- **Where IAM's Law enters:** Not the law: a chain rule.

### 22. The Locator (where it changed: places and genes)

- **In the field's terms:** Differential methylation at regions and genes (DMRs and DMGs), called per sample against a healthy reference, with gene annotation
- **Reads from:** both: places for the molecule instruments come from molecules, places for the counts instruments from counts
- **What it measures and how:** Per-place observed versus expected counts against an empirical healthy null with Benjamini-Hochberg control, annotated with CpG island, gene and promoter/gene-body/nearby relation from UCSC hg19 tracks
- **Where IAM's Law enters:** .
- **Credit:** Positions and genes: UCSC Genome Browser (Kent et al. 2002, Genome Res. 12:996-1006, doi 10.1101/gr.229102); NCBI RefSeq (O'Leary et al. 2016, Nucleic Acids Res. 44:D733-D745); UCSC known genes (Hsu et al. 2006, Bioinformatics 22:1036-1046). CpG islands: Gardiner-Garden & Frommer 1987 (J. Mol. Biol. 196:261-282), the definition of the UCSC track; shores: Irizarry et al. 2009 (Nat. Genet. 41:178-186). Promoter window and shore/shelf definitions as used by Koldobskiy et al. 2021 (Nat. Biomed. Eng.), so gene lists compare directly. False-discovery control: Benjamini & Hochberg 1995 (J. R. Stat. Soc. B 57:289-300). CpG numbering: wgbstools (Loyfer et al. 2023, Nature 613:355-364). IAM (this work): calling places per sample against the healthy atlas at the sample's own depth and mix, with a measured healthy null and a measured detection limit.

#### The Locator: naming the places that changed, and the genes there

*Status:* development

- **How it works:** For each instrument, every place it reads (an island or block for the Law Sphere and the counts; a region for the globe) is tested: the sample's count at the place against the count the healthy atlas expects there at the sample's own read depth and cell mix, judged against the spread measured among healthy libraries (not counting alone), with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery control across that instrument's places. Each place named is given its chromosome and position, its CpG island context (island, shore, shelf, open sea), its genes (promoter: within 2 kb of a transcription start; gene body; or the nearest gene and its distance), and whether any array probe covers it.
- **Why:** A score says how much a sample changed; a researcher also needs to know where, and which genes, to compare with expression, with other studies and across patients.
- **The numbers:** 592,067 places (CpG islands, then 50-CpG blocks) and 28,218 regions; places by RefSeq relation: promoter 104,607, gene body 254,895, intergenic 232,565; by context: island 95,089, shore 35,892, shelf 21,335, open sea 439,751; 18,755 promoter places without an array probe. Planted tests on GSM5652214: 9 of 10 gain islands found, loss blocks named at 6.3 times their healthy level and above, none below 3.3; no place named in any healthy or unplanted read (every loss and gain unit tested).
- **Method and standard:** Positions reference built from public UCSC hg19 files and checked against all 813,951 array probe positions; healthy null by leave-one-out over the 205 atlas libraries; planted-place tests for detection.
- **Limits:** Detection depends on depth: at about 30-fold, a loss block expecting about 5 held errors is named once it shows about 4 to 6 times that (finding ); each report prints its own sample's limit, so 'nothing found' is read against it. Promoter calls depend on the gene table (both kept). Positions are hg19.
- **How to rebuild it:** python3 'chain/Runtime Matrices/Where/build_where_ref.py' hg19.fa.gz cpgIslandExt.txt.gz refGene.txt.gz sites_sequencing_key.parquet units.npz OUT; then build_where_genes_v2.py OUT refGene.txt.gz knownGene.txt.gz kgXref.txt.gz cpgIslandExt.txt.gz OUT (public UCSC hg19 files from hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu; both builds check themselves and stop on any disagreement)
- **Files in the repository:** [build_where_ref.py](https://github.com/hmahaffeyges/IAM-Validation/blob/main/Biological_Physics/MethylPhys/chain/Runtime%20Matrices/Where/build_where_ref.py), [build_where_genes_v2.py](https://github.com/hmahaffeyges/IAM-Validation/blob/main/Biological_Physics/MethylPhys/chain/Runtime%20Matrices/Where/build_where_genes_v2.py), [README.md](https://github.com/hmahaffeyges/IAM-Validation/blob/main/Biological_Physics/MethylPhys/chain/Runtime%20Matrices/Where/README.md), [where_ref_v2.json](https://github.com/hmahaffeyges/IAM-Validation/blob/main/Biological_Physics/MethylPhys/chain/Runtime%20Matrices/Where/where_ref_v2.json)

*Questions a researcher will ask:*

- **How do you know a named place is not just noise?** Each place is judged against how far healthy libraries actually stray there (measured on the 205 atlas libraries), not against counting alone, with false-discovery control. In every healthy and unplanted read so far, no place was named; planted places were found (9 of 10 planted gains; loss blocks at 6.3 times their healthy level and above). *(Evidence: findings)*
- **Why do the gene calls follow one study's definitions?** So named genes compare directly with that study's published gene lists: promoter within 2 kb of a transcription start, shores within 2 kb of an island, shelves 2 to 4 kb. Both RefSeq and the UCSC known-genes table are given, since the second calls more promoters. *(Evidence: a chain update; finding)*
- **What does 'array-blind' mean for a gene?** No array probe covers that place, so no array study could have measured it. 18,755 of the Locator's promoter places (RefSeq) have no probe. *(Evidence: finding)*

- **IAM's name:** Positions reference v1
- **In the field's terms:** Positions reference v1
- **Definition:** every place's chromosome, start and end, CpG count, array probe count and CpG island

- **Credit:** Positions and genes: UCSC Genome Browser (Kent et al. 2002, Genome Res. 12:996-1006, doi 10.1101/gr.229102); NCBI RefSeq (O'Leary et al. 2016, Nucleic Acids Res. 44:D733-D745); UCSC known genes (Hsu et al. 2006, Bioinformatics 22:1036-1046).
